p.src: Now Kan Ze, whose courtesy name was Derun, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji. His family was poor, but he loved learning; he hired himself out as a laborer and often borrowed other people's books to read. Once he had read something through, he never forgot it. He was eloquent and quick-witted, and possessed uncommon courage. Sun Quan summoned him to serve as an adviser, and he became especially close to Huang Gai. Huang Gai knew that he was eloquent and courageous, and therefore wished him to deliver the false letter of surrender. Kan Ze gladly agreed, saying, “If a true man passes through life without winning merit or founding an achievement, is he not little better than grass and trees that rot away together? Since you are ready to sacrifice yourself in repayment of our lord, why should I begrudge my insignificant life?” Huang Gai rolled out of bed, bowed, and thanked him. Kan Ze said, “The matter admits no delay. I shall leave at once.” Huang Gai said, “The letter is already written.”

p.src: Kan Ze took the letter and, that very night, disguised himself as a fisherman, boarded a small boat, and made for the northern bank. The cold stars filled the sky that night, and by the third watch he had already reached Cao Cao's naval camp. The soldiers patrolling the river seized him and reported to Cao Cao that same night. Cao Cao said, “Could he be a spy?” The soldier replied, “He is only a fisherman, but calls himself Kan Ze, an adviser of Eastern Wu, and says he has come on confidential business.” Cao Cao ordered that he be brought in. The soldiers led Kan Ze inside. The lamps and candles in the tent shone brilliantly, while Cao Cao sat erect behind his table and asked, “Since you are an adviser of Eastern Wu, what brings you here?” Kan Ze said, “People say that Chancellor Cao thirsts for worthy men, but judging from that question, the report is far from true. Huang Gongfu, you too have badly misjudged him!”

p.src: At his table Cao Cao turned the letter over and read it more than ten times. Suddenly he struck the table, opened his eyes wide in fury, and cried, “Huang Gai has used the ruse of self-inflicted suffering and sent you with a false letter of surrender to seize an opportunity for some scheme. How dare you come here and make sport of me!” He ordered his attendants to drag Kan Ze out and behead him. The attendants crowded around Kan Ze and hustled him away, but his expression did not change; he threw back his head and laughed aloud. Cao Cao had him brought back and rebuked him: “I have seen through your treacherous scheme. Why do you laugh?” Kan Ze said, “I am not laughing at you. I am laughing only because Huang Gongfu cannot judge men.” Cao Cao asked, “How can he not judge men?” Kan Ze said, “If you mean to kill me, then kill me. Why ask so many questions?” Cao Cao said, “From childhood I have studied the military classics thoroughly and know the ways of deceit and falsehood well. This scheme of yours might deceive others, but how could it deceive me?” Kan Ze said, “Then tell me: what in the letter constitutes a treacherous scheme?” Cao Cao said, “I shall point out the flaw in your story, so that you may die without complaint! If this letter truly offers surrender in good faith, why does it not clearly appoint a time? What argument can you make now?”

p.src: When Kan Ze had heard him out, he laughed loudly and said, “It is remarkable that you feel no shame, yet dare boast that you have studied the military classics thoroughly! Why do you not withdraw your army and return while there is still time? If you give battle, Zhou Yu will surely capture you! Ignorant fool! What a pity that I should die unjustly at your hands!” Cao Cao asked, “Why do you call me ignorant?” Kan Ze said, “You understand neither stratagem nor reason. Are you not ignorant, then?” Cao Cao said, “Then tell me in what respects I am wrong.” Kan Ze said, “You show no courtesy in receiving worthy men. Why should I say anything? There is nothing left but death.” Cao Cao said, “If your explanation is reasonable, I shall naturally respect and accept it.” Kan Ze said, “Have you never heard the saying, ‘One who betrays his lord and acts in secret cannot fix a date’? If we fixed a date now, but he suddenly found himself unable to act, while your side came to receive him as arranged, the entire affair would inevitably be exposed. He can only watch for an opportunity and act. How could a date be set beforehand? You do not understand this principle and would put an innocent man to an unjust death. You truly are an ignorant fool!”

p.src: On hearing this, Cao Cao changed his manner, descended from his seat, and apologized: “I failed to perceive the matter clearly and mistakenly offended your dignity. I hope you will not take it to heart.” Kan Ze said, “Huang Gongfu and I surrender to you with all our hearts, as infants yearn for their parents. How could there be any deceit?” Cao Cao was delighted and said, “If you two can render great service, the ranks you receive hereafter will surely stand above those of all others.” Kan Ze said, “We have not come for rank or emolument, but truly to answer Heaven's will and follow the wishes of the people.” Cao Cao brought out wine and entertained him.

p.src: A short while later, someone entered the tent and whispered privately in Cao Cao's ear. Cao Cao said, “Bring me the letter.” The man presented a secret letter. Cao Cao read it, and his face showed considerable pleasure. Kan Ze thought to himself, “This must be Cai Zhong and Cai He reporting that Huang Gai has been punished. Cao Cao is therefore pleased that my account of the surrender has proved true.” Cao Cao said, “May I trouble you, sir, to return once more to Jiangdong and arrange matters with Huang Gongfu? Have him send word across the river beforehand, and I shall dispatch troops to receive him.” Kan Ze said, “I have already left Jiangdong and cannot return there. I ask Your Excellency to send some other trusted agent.” Cao Cao said, “If another goes, I fear the matter may be exposed.” Kan Ze declined again and again, but after a long while said, “If I must go, I dare not remain here any longer. I shall depart at once.”

p.src: Cao Cao bestowed gold and silk on him, but Kan Ze refused them. He took his leave, departed the camp, and again boarded his little boat. Returning to Jiangdong, he went to see Huang Gai and related everything that had happened in detail. Huang Gai said, “Had it not been for your eloquence, my suffering would have been in vain.” Kan Ze said, “I shall now go to Gan Ning's camp and sound out Cai Zhong and Cai He.” Huang Gai said, “Excellent.” Kan Ze reached Gan Ning's camp, and Gan Ning received him inside. Kan Ze said, “Yesterday, General, you were humiliated by Zhou Gongjin for trying to save Huang Gongfu. I find it deeply unjust.” Gan Ning smiled but did not answer.

p.src: While they were talking, Cai He and Cai Zhong arrived. Kan Ze signaled Gan Ning with his eyes. Gan Ning understood and said, “Zhou Gongjin relies entirely on his own ability and shows no consideration whatever for men like us. Now that I have been humiliated, I am ashamed to face the people of Jiangdong!” When he had finished, he ground his teeth, struck the table, and shouted. Kan Ze then pretended to whisper in Gan Ning's ear. Gan Ning lowered his head without speaking and heaved several long sighs.

Gan Ning drew his sword, sprang to his feet, and cried, “Our affair has already been discovered. We must kill them to silence them!”

p.src: Cai He and Cai Zhong said in alarm, “You two gentlemen need not worry. We too have a confidential matter to disclose.” Gan Ning said, “Tell us at once!” Cai He said, “The two of us were sent by Lord Cao to feign surrender. If you gentlemen intend to submit to him, we shall introduce you.” Gan Ning asked, “Is what you say really true?” The two replied in unison, “How would we dare deceive you?” Gan Ning feigned delight and said, “If so, Heaven itself has granted us this opportunity!” The two Cais said, “We have already informed the Prime Minister how General Huang Gongfu and you were humiliated.” Kan Ze said, “I have already delivered a letter to the Prime Minister on Huang Gongfu’s behalf. I came especially to see Xingba and arrange for us to surrender together.” Gan Ning said, “Once a true man encounters an enlightened lord, he should naturally devote himself wholeheartedly to him.” Thereupon the four drank together and spoke openly of what was in their hearts. The two Cais immediately wrote a secret report to Cao Cao, saying that Gan Ning and the other man would serve together as agents within the enemy camp. Kan Ze composed a separate letter and sent a man to report secretly to Cao Cao. The letter explained in full that Huang Gai wished to come but had not yet found an opportunity; the vessel approaching with a blue pennant at its prow would be his.

p.src: Now Cao Cao received both letters in succession. Still beset by doubts, he assembled his advisers and said, “Gan Ning of the lands east of the river, having been humiliated by Zhou Yu, offers to act as our agent within his camp; and Huang Gai, after being punished, has sent Kan Ze to offer his surrender. Neither can yet be trusted fully. Who dares go straight into Zhou Yu’s camp and ascertain the truth?” Jiang Gan stepped forward and said, “The other day I went to the Southland in vain and accomplished nothing, for which I remain deeply ashamed. Now I am willing to risk my life and go again. I shall obtain the truth without fail and report it to you, Prime Minister.” Cao Cao was delighted and immediately ordered Jiang Gan to board a vessel. Jiang Gan sailed a small boat directly to the edge of the southern naval camp and sent a man ahead to announce him.

p.src: When Zhou Yu heard that Jiang Gan had returned, he was overjoyed. “My success depends entirely upon this man!” he said. He then instructed Lu Su, “Invite Pang Shiyuan here and have him do thus and so for me.” Pang Tong of Xiangyang, whose courtesy name was Shiyuan, had in fact taken refuge in the Southland to escape the turmoil. Lu Su had once recommended him to Zhou Yu, but Pang Tong had not yet gone to meet him. Zhou Yu had first sent Lu Su to ask Pang Tong for a plan: “What strategy should we use to defeat Cao Cao?” Pang Tong told Lu Su privately, “To defeat Cao Cao’s forces, you must attack them with fire; but on the broad river, once one vessel catches fire, all the others will scatter. Only by presenting a ‘chain-link stratagem’ and inducing him to fasten all his vessels together can the plan succeed.” Lu Su reported this to Zhou Yu, who greatly admired the proposal and said to him, “The only man who can execute this plan for me is Pang Shiyuan.” Lu Su said, “I fear only that Cao Cao is too cunning. How can he be approached?”

p.src: Zhou Yu pondered without reaching a decision. Just as he wondered how an opportunity might be found, word suddenly came that Jiang Gan had returned. Zhou Yu was delighted. On the one hand, he instructed Pang Tong to carry out the stratagem; on the other, he seated himself in his tent and sent someone to summon Jiang Gan. When Jiang Gan saw that no one came to welcome him, doubts arose in his mind. He ordered his boat moored at a secluded stretch of the bank, then entered the camp to see Zhou Yu. Zhou Yu scowled and said, “Ziyi, why did you deceive me so outrageously?” Jiang Gan laughed. “I thought that you and I were old friends, and came especially to confide my innermost thoughts. How can you accuse me of deception?” Zhou Yu said, “If you mean to persuade me to surrender, that will happen only when the seas run dry and the rocks crumble! Last time, for the sake of our old friendship, I invited you to drink your fill, let you sleep beside me, yet you stole my private letter and departed without farewell, then returned and reported to Cao Cao, causing him to kill Cai Mao and Zhang Yun and thereby thwarting my design. Why have you come again today? You surely harbor no good intention! Were it not for our former friendship, I would cut you in two with a single stroke! I had intended to send you back across the river, but within a day or two I mean to destroy the traitor Cao; yet if I keep you in the army, our secrets will inevitably leak.” He then ordered his attendants, “Escort Ziyi to the hermitage in the western hills to rest. After I have defeated Cao Cao, it will not be too late to ferry you across the river.”

p.src: Jiang Gan was about to speak again, but Zhou Yu had already withdrawn behind the tent. The attendants brought Jiang Gan a horse and escorted him to a small hermitage behind the western hills, assigning two soldiers to wait upon him. In the hermitage, Jiang Gan was so troubled at heart that he could neither sleep nor eat in peace. That night, beneath a sky filled with stars and dew, he walked alone behind the hermitage and heard someone reading aloud. Following the sound at an idle pace, he saw several thatched rooms beside a rocky cliff, with lamplight shining from within. Jiang Gan peered inside and saw a man who had hung his sword before the lamp and was reciting the military writings of Sun and Wu. Thinking that this must be an extraordinary man, Jiang Gan knocked at the door and requested an audience. The man opened the door and came out to welcome him. His bearing was far from ordinary. When Jiang Gan asked his name, he replied, “My family name is Pang, my given name Tong, and my courtesy name Shiyuan.” Jiang Gan asked, “Can you be none other than Master Young Phoenix?” Pang Tong replied, “I am.” Jiang Gan said joyfully, “I have long heard your great name. Why do you now live in seclusion here?” He answered, “Zhou Yu prides himself on his great talent and cannot tolerate others. That is why I live here in seclusion. And who might you be, sir?” Jiang Gan replied, “I am Jiang Gan.”

u.src: Thus he and Jiang Gan descended the mountain that very night, found the original boat at the riverbank, and rowed swiftly toward the northern shore.
Upon reaching Cao Cao’s camp, Jiang Gan went in first and related the whole course of events.

When Cao Cao heard that Master Young Phoenix had come, he personally left his tent to welcome him. Once host and guest had taken their places, Cao Cao said, “Zhou Yu is young, and relying on his talent, he treats others with contempt and rejects sound counsel.
I have long heard of your great reputation, sir. Now that you have honored me with your presence, I beg you not to withhold your instruction.”
Pang Tong replied, “I have always heard that the Prime Minister conducts war according to sound principles. I should now like to behold the disposition of your forces.”

p.src: Cao Cao ordered horses prepared and first invited Pang Tong to inspect the land encampment with him. Pang Tong and Cao Cao rode side by side to high ground and looked out over the camp. Pang Tong said, “It stands beside the hills and against the woods; front and rear support each other; its entrances and exits are properly gated; its avenues for advance and retreat wind with artful complexity. Even if Sun Wu were reborn or Rangju returned to life, they could devise nothing beyond this.” Cao Cao said, “You must not praise me beyond my merits, sir. I still hope for your instruction.” They then went together to inspect the naval camp. Facing south were twenty-four gateways, each guarded by warships and fighting vessels arranged like city walls. Smaller boats lay sheltered within, lanes allowed passage back and forth, and every rise and fall followed an ordered pattern. Pang Tong laughed and said, “The Prime Minister’s renown in warfare is truly deserved!” Then he pointed toward the southern bank and cried, “Zhou Yu! Zhou Yu! Your doom is sealed for the appointed day!”

p.src: Cao Cao returned to camp in great delight, invited Pang Tong into his tent, and set out wine for them to drink as they discussed the art of war. Pang Tong discoursed loftily and argued with vigor, answering every question with effortless fluency. Cao Cao admired him deeply and treated him with the utmost courtesy. Pang Tong pretended to be drunk and asked, “May I ask whether there are skilled physicians in the army?” Cao Cao asked why he needed one. Pang Tong replied, “Many of the naval troops are ill and require skilled physicians to treat them.” At the time, Cao Cao’s soldiers were unaccustomed to the climate and water. They suffered from vomiting, and many had died. Cao Cao was already anxious about this matter. Hearing Pang Tong mention it, how could he fail to inquire further? Pang Tong said, “The Prime Minister’s method of training the naval forces is excellent, but unfortunately it is incomplete.” Cao Cao repeatedly pressed him for an explanation. Pang Tong said, “I have a plan by which every man in the naval forces, high and low, may remain free from illness and victory may be achieved securely.”

p.src: Cao Cao was delighted and asked him to explain this ingenious plan. Pang Tong said, “On the Great River, the tides rise and fall and the wind and waves never cease. The northern troops are unused to traveling by ship; tossed about like this, they soon fall ill. But if the large and small vessels are joined together, perhaps thirty in a row or perhaps fifty, linked from bow to stern with iron rings and chains and covered with broad planks, then not only men but even horses could cross over them. Sailing aboard these, you could let the wind, waves, and tides rise and fall as they pleased—what would there be left to fear?” Cao Cao left his seat and thanked him, saying, “Without your excellent counsel, sir, how could I defeat the Southland?” Pang Tong said, “It is merely my humble opinion. p.src: Pang Tong further said to Cao Cao, “From what I have seen, many of the heroes east of the river bear grudges against Zhou Yu. With my glib tongue, I shall persuade them on your behalf and induce them all to surrender. Zhou Yu, isolated and without aid, will surely be captured by you. Once Zhou Yu is defeated, Liu Bei will be of no further consequence.” Cao Cao said, “If you truly accomplish this great feat, sir, I shall report it to the Son of Heaven and have you appointed to the ranks of the Three Excellencies.” Pang Tong said, “I do not seek wealth or rank; I wish only to save the common people. When you cross the river, Prime Minister, take care that no one is killed.” Cao Cao said, “I act on Heaven’s behalf to uphold the Way. How could I bear to slaughter the people?” Pang Tong bowed and requested a proclamation to ensure the safety of his clan. Cao Cao asked, “Where does your family presently live, sir?” Pang Tong replied, “They live beside the river. With such a proclamation, their safety can be assured.”

p.src: Cao Cao ordered the proclamation written, countersigned it, and handed it to Pang Tong. Pang Tong bowed his thanks and said, “After I leave, advance your forces swiftly. Do not wait until Zhou Yu discovers what is happening.” Cao Cao agreed.

p.src: Pang Tong took his leave and went to the riverbank. Just as he was about to board a boat, he suddenly saw a man on the shore dressed in a Daoist robe and bamboo cap. The man seized him and said, “What audacity you have! Huang Gai employs the ruse of self-inflicted suffering, Kan Ze delivers a false letter of surrender, and now you come to offer the linked-ships stratagem—all for fear that the fire might not burn everything to ashes! Such ruthless schemes may deceive Cao Cao, but you cannot deceive me!” Pang Tong was so terrified that his soul nearly fled his body. Indeed:
